narrative: Three days of data now show network difficulty and reward stepping down together (difficulty ~33.2M → 31.6M → 29.3M; block time 356s → 402s) since the July 23 dense-only PoW fork — consistent with hashrate normalizing down from the MoE-exploit-inflated highs toward a more real baseline, not a network health problem. DEX volume thinned sharply ($12.6k → $2.0k) and price eased -2.4%, both unremarkable day-to-day swings on modest liquidity. Bridge custody is essentially flat (+0.08%). Social mentions jumped to 167, but the increase is templated pump-signal spam bots, not organic interest — see social summary. GitHub activity ticked up (8 commits combined) reflecting yesterday's next→main merge landing in the tracked repo.

anomalies: The /api/supply-vs-custody discrepancy is back (197 PRL this time: 1,018,152.94 vs 1,017,955.94), having read clean yesterday and 126 PRL off the day before. Confirmed via a retry two seconds apart (unchanged), so it's not a mid-update race — looks like an intermittent quirk in the relay's supply endpoint rather than a one-off. Worth a dev look if it keeps recurring.

Deposit/burn volume both thinned sharply (37,869 → 18,812 → 1,759 PRL deposits over three days) — ordinary daily variance, not a bridge issue; custody and supply both remain internally consistent aside from the discrepancy noted above.
Fast-lane usage reads 0% because this snapshot lands moments after the daily UTC window reset — same pattern as prior runs, not a usage drop.

Pearlbridge's own account kept its regular dev-education cadence (trust model, wrap/unwrap mechanics, no-interest clarification). One organic mining-community comment noted difficulty easing, consistent with what this snapshot's own block data shows. As always, a distinct "Perle Labs" project sharing the PRL ticker (a treasury-unlock announcement today) is unrelated to Pearl Network and excluded.

incidents.summary: Pearl's July 1 MoE (mixture-of-experts) PoW extension had an economic-pricing bug: sparse expert-routed proofs were credited as full dense-difficulty work, letting miners claim outsized rewards without proportional real compute (not proof forgery, no PearlBridge custody impact, and DeFiLlama's hack database lists nothing for Pearl). Reported network hashrate rose from ~30 EH/s to 90+ EH/s over three weeks as this was exploited. The core team activated a dense-only PoW fork at mainnet height ~91,630 to shut off MoE crediting, with a same-day hotfix for a template-classification bug in the fork logic itself. Current chain height (91,737) is past the fork — the fix is live.

MinePRL, the canonical community pool tracked by this dashboard, is offline (site redirects visitors to prlscan.com); exact offline date within the past ~6 weeks is unconfirmed. Network hashrate and pool worker-count fields are null this snapshot pending a replacement public data source.
